text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam will help Laos implement a roughly $145,000 project to tackle malaria, Vietnam's Public Health Minister Do Nguyen Phuong said.
-- Vietnam has asked China to immediately withdraw its drilling rig, the Kan Tan III, from Vietnam's Continental Shelf.
-- The Ministry of Industry has shut down a series of loss-making gemstone mines owned by the Viet-Thai Joint Venture Company in the northern province of Yen Bai.
-- The Ministry of Interior has set up an narcotics squad to prevent trafficking and drug abuse and also an anti-terrorist squad.
-- The journey time on the north-south express train has been cut to 34 hours from 36.
-- Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will visit Vietnam on March 30-31. - - - -
-- The value of exports from Ho Chi Minh City was more than $392 million in the first two months of 1997. Full-year 1996 exports came to $3.72 billion.
-- The leader of a Hanoi crime syndicate was sentenced to 9-1/2 years in prison. Other gangs were sentenced to prison terms ranging from three months to six years. - - - -
-- U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin will visit Vietnam from April 6 to 8.
